museum.museumAddress:
Franz Marc Park
82431 Kochel, Germany
museum.museumOverview: This museum was founded in 1986 to showcase Franz Marc's life and work within the setting and landscape that so influenced him. Since 2008, the facility has displayed Marc's works juxtaposed with examples of his contemporaries. Its permanent collection includes key works by Paul Klee, along with major post-war German and French art.

museum.museumAddress:
1 East 70th Street
New York, New York 10021
museum.museumOverview: Assembled by the Pittsburgh industrialist Henry Clay Frick, this collection lives in the Frick family’s former Fifth Avenue residence overlooking Central Park; it's one of New York City’s few remaining Gilded Age mansions. The setting is transcendent, as are the masterpieces by Giovanni Bellini, Rembrandt, Johannes Vermeer, Thomas Gainsborough, Francisco Goya and James Whistler, among others. Also on display are outstanding examples of European sculpture and decorative arts. The museum opened in 1935, and today offers a wide range of special exhibitions, lectures, symposia and educational programmes that foster a deeper appreciation of this special collection.

museum.museumAddress:
Carrer Aragó, 255
08007 Barcelona, Spain
museum.museumOverview: This foundation was created in 1984 by artist Antoni Tàpies to promote the study and knowledge of Modern and contemporary art. The Fundació takes a pluralistic, interdisciplinary approach: it sets up cooperative ventures with experts in different fields in order to contribute to a better understanding of contemporary art and culture. The Fundació owns one of the world’s most complete collections of Tàpies’ work, which mainly consists of donations by Antoni and Teresa Tàpies. It augments periodic presentations of the artist’s work with temporary exhibitions, symposia, lectures, films and a range of publications. The museum opened its doors in June 1990 in the building of the former Editorial Montaner i Simon publishing house, designed by Modernist architect Lluís Domènech i Montaner.

museum.museumAddress:
Parc de Montjuïc
08038 Barcelona, Spain
museum.museumOverview: Formed between Joan Miró and friend Joan Prats, the Joan Miró Foundation sought to encourage younger artists to experiment with contemporary art, while also ensuring that contemporary pieces remain available to the public. The Foundation brought a refreshing vitality together with a more dynamic concept of an art museum in which Miró’s art was shown alongside a wide variety of creative works by other artists.

museum.museumAddress:
Miguel de Cervantes Saavedra 303
Colonia Ampliación Granada
11529 Mexcio City, Mexico
museum.museumOverview: This museum, in the main exhibition space of the Fundación Jumex Arte Contemporáneo, opened in November 2013 in a stunning building designed by British architect David Chipperfield. The structure, which features local materials that pay homage to the environment of Mexico City, is Mr Chipperfield’s first project in Latin America. The permanent contemporary art collection – one of Mexico’s most important – as well as changing exhibitions populate five storeys of a remarkable facility that totals an impressive 6,700 square metres.

museum.museumAddress:
La Boca, Caminito
C1169AAD Buenos Aires, Argentina
museum.museumOverview: This centre for contemporary art is located in La Boca, a vibrant community just south of Buenos Aires. Since 1996, the foundation has played a significant role in revitalising the country's artistic profile through its compelling programmes and exhibitions, which regularly bring major international works to the Argentinian public. The scope embraces three areas: Argentinian and Latin American art, international, historical and contemporary art and finally, emerging art. Its location and architecture juxtapose contemporary design with the local landscape and aesthetic, while the centre itself supports curatorial projects that find new ways to engage the community.

museum.museumAddress: 800 W Olympic Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90015
museum.museumOverview:
The GRAMMY Museum explores and celebrates the enduring legacies of all forms of music, with an emphasis on the creative process of music-making; the art and technology of the recording process; and the history of the GRAMMY Awards, the premier recognition of recorded music accomplishment. The Museum boasts a variety of interactive and exciting permanent and temporary exhibitions that highlight the significance of American music with the hope of inspiring the next generation to explore and create music using the country's centuries-old musical roots. 

Present your Preferred card at the Museum's box office for complimentary entry, and to ensure your parking can be validated, please enter the L.A. LIVE district parking via the East Garage parking lot, located at the intersection of Olympic Blvd. and Francisco St. Should you be interested in a tour of the museum please kindly enquire.

museum.museumAddress:
9/23 Krymsky Val St.
119049, Moscow, Russia
museum.museumOverview: Founded in 2008 by Dasha Zhukova and Roman Abramovich, Garage is the first philanthropic organization in Russia devoted to contemporary art and culture. The institution reflects on current developments in Russian and international culture, as well as the production of new work and ideas in Moscow. At the center of its extensive programme of exhibitions, events and research & publication is the Museum’s collection, the first archive in the country related to the development of Russian contemporary art from the 1950s through the present. Initially housed in the renowned Bakhmetevsky Bus Garage in Moscow, Garage relocated in 2015 to its permanent home, the former Gorky Park Vremena Goda, transformed and designed by Rem Koolhaas and his OMA studio.

museum.museumAddress:
217 Johnson Street
Santa Fe, NM 87501
museum.museumOverview: Located in Santa Fe, New Mexico, this museum presents a series of galleries organized by theme to offer a deeper understanding the artistic legacy of Georgia O'Keeffe (1887-1986), as well as the study and interpretations of North American Modernism. Through installations and educational platforms, visitors can explore a remarkable American story through O’Keeffe’s art, art materials and personal possessions, along with photographs and documents from her life. In addition, the Museum owns O’Keeffe’s Home and Studio in Abiquiu, New Mexico, which is open seasonally for tours by reservation. Also noteworthy: this is the only museum in the world dedicated to a female artist from North America.

museum.museumAddress:
3, Avenue Du General Eisenhower
75008 Paris, France
museum.museumOverview:
Each year, the Réunion des Musées Nationaux – Grand Palais (Rmn-GP) presents approximately 40 highly diverse cultural events in Paris, other parts of France and abroad. The Grand Palais, a favourite monument of the French, is the institution’s prestigious showcase located in the heart of Paris. Its programming includes exhibitions, concerts, fashion shows, salons and performances, and strives to be serious yet accessible to all audiences. In addition to events, the Rmn-GP exerts influence through a publishing arm and network of bookstores and shops, as well as its photo agency, which is France’s most important source for art images. The Rmn-GP also helps to enrich national collections by carrying out acquisitions on behalf of the French State.

museum.museumAddress:
Glockengiesserwall
20095 Hamburg, Germany
museum.museumOverview: The Hamburger Kunsthalle is one of the largest and most important art museums in Germany. Its superb permanent collection takes visitors on a journey through seven centuries of art, from the medieval altars of Master Bertram to contemporary art world stars including Gerhard Richter and Neo Rauch. Among the highlights of the collection are Dutch paintings of the 17th century, including works by Rembrandt Harmenszoon van Rijn and Jacob van Ruisdael, German paintings of the Romantic period with extensive groups of works by Caspar David Friedrich and Philipp Otto Runge, as well as important paintings by Adolph Menzel and Max Liebermann.

museum.museumAddress:
Southbank Centre
London SE1 8XX
United Kingdom
museum.museumOverview: As part of Southbank Centre, in the heart of one of London’s most thriving cultural quarters, the Hayward Gallery displays a wide range of contemporary and Modern art. Its cutting-edge and groundbreaking exhibitions often feature nationally and internationally renowned artists. The gallery manages the Arts Council Collection, which is one of the largest loan collections of Modern and contemporary art in the world – comprising more than 7,500 works of art by generations of British artists.

museum.museumAddress:
4155 Linnean Ave. NW
Washington, DC 20008
museum.museumOverview: Opened in 1977, Hillwood Estate, Museum and Gardens is an immersive space where the captivating life of Marjorie Merriweather Post and the exquisitely maintained Mansion and Gardens combine to create an experience unlike any other. When art collector, businesswoman, social figure and philanthropist Marjorie Post left to the public her northwest Washington, DC estate, she endowed the country with the most comprehensive collection of Russian imperial art outside of Russia, an exquisite eighteenth-century French decorative art collection, twenty-five acres of serene landscaped gardens and natural woodlands and a pristine Georgian-style mansion displaying Post's exquisite way of life. Highlights of the collection include Fabergé eggs, Russian porcelain, Russian Orthodox icons, Beauvais tapestries, Sèvres porcelain and Post’s personal collection of apparel, accessories and jewellery. The thirteen acres of enchanting formal gardens include a Japanese-style garden, rose garden, French parterre and greenhouse full of orchids. A range of special exhibitions are presented throughout the year to offer added perspectives on the collections, gardens and founder's life story.

museum.museumAddress:
100 Northern Avenue
Boston, Massachusetts 02210
museum.museumOverview: Founded in 1936, this is one of the country’s leading destinations for contemporary art, performance and film. Award-winning architects Diller Scofidio + Renfro designed the iconic building on Boston Harbor, weaving together interior and exterior spaces to create shifting perspectives of the waterfront throughout the galleries and public spaces. Similarly, the institute's exhibitions and programmes aim to offer new ways of engaging with the world: they provide access to contemporary artists and the creative process, and invite audiences of all ages and backgrounds to participate in the excitement surrounding new art and ideas.

The Tapestry Room, restored in 2011, is home to a spectacular series of 16th-century Flemish tapestries, among other works of art. Photograph by Sean Dungan, 2011

museum.museumAddress:
25 Evans Way,
Boston, Massachusetts 02115
museum.museumOverview:
Opened to the public in 1903, the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum continues its founding mission to celebrate personal connections with art. Located in an intimate Venetian-inspired palace in the heart of Boston with three floors of gorgeous galleries surrounding a flower-filled courtyard, this museum is home to more than 2,500 art objects spanning 30 centuries. Of special interest are masterpieces by Sandro Botticelli, Titian, Raphael, Rembrandt, Edgar Degas and John Singer Sargent. Supplementing this impressive permanent collection are historical and contemporary special exhibitions, an artist-in-residence programme, concerts and public events. The museum continues to grow: a new wing designed by Renzo Piano opened in 2012.


Photograph: © Nic Lehoux, 2012

museum.museumAddress:
11 Ruppin Boulevard
Jerusalem, Israel 9171002
museum.museumOverview: Established in 1965, Israel's largest cultural institution is also ranked among the world’s leading art and archaeology museums. In addition, it features a large collection of paintings representing a wide range of periods, styles, subjects and regions. Painters in the collection include such international figures as Rembrandt, Marc Chagall and Camille Pissarro, as well as Israeli and Jewish artists including Abel Pann and Reuven Rubin. The Israel Museum also operates two off-site locations: the Rockefeller Archaeological Museum, an architectural gem built in 1938 to display archaeology from ancient Israel, and Ticho House, which offers an ongoing programme of exhibitions by younger Israeli artists within an historic house and garden setting.

museum.museumAddress:
Liman İşletmeleri  Sahası Antrepo D:4

34433 Istanbul, Turkey
museum.museumOverview:
The Istanbul Modern, Turkey’s first private museum to organize modern and contemporary art exhibitions, was founded in 2004 and occupies an 8,000 square meter site on the shores of the Bosphorus.

The Istanbul Modern presents a wide variety of works ranging from painting and sculpture to installation and video, from the early 20th century to our day.  Istanbul Modern’s permanent collection features Turkey’s evolution of modern and contemporary art by showcasing works by prominent artists in chronological order.  The texts accompanying the works explain the social, cultural, economic, and political dynamics of this process.  The museum additionally brings together works by prominent representatives of contemporary art from both Turkey and different countries.

museum.museumAddress:
1109 Fifth Avenue
New York, New York 10128
museum.museumOverview: Located in the heart of New York City’s famed Museum Mile, this institution has the largest collection of Jewish art and cultural objects outside Israel, with 26,000 pieces in all. Furthermore, it occupies a unique niche in the city’s cultural landscape as a museum of art, culture and ideas. In the 1960s, the museum took a more active role within the larger world of contemporary art with exhibitions including Primary Structures, which helped to launch the Minimalist art movement. In the decades since, however, the museum has renewed its focus on Jewish artists and culture, while still maintaining a strong allegiance to Modern and contemporary art with its exciting temporary exhibitions.

museum.museumAddress:
Dorotheergasse 11 & Judenplatz 8
1010 Vienna, Austria
museum.museumOverview: This museum is divided into two locations, Jewish Museum Dorotheergasse and Judenplatz. Both offer unique overviews of Viennese Jewish history and today’s vibrant Jewish community. Rachel Whiteread’s Holocaust Memorial in front of the Museum Judenplatz, Nancy Spero’s installations in the Museum Dorotheergasse and a permanent installation from well-known Austrian artist Brigitte Kowanz represent just a few examples of the importance of contemporary art to the Jewish Museum Vienna.

museum.museumAddress: 2 Jin Sha Yi Zhi Lu, Chengdu, China
museum.museumOverview: The first major archeological discovery in China at the beginning of the 21st century, the Jinsha site is considered one of the most significant discoveries on the ancient Shu civilisation of the Shu Kingdom. Jinsha site have uncovered a large amount of artefacts, including gold, jade and ivory. To date, the Sun and Immortal Bird Gold Ornament is the most important artefact unearthed at the site, and its pattern was selected both as the emblem for Chinese Cultural Heritage and the Chengdu city logo.
